nodes.label: On the Scaling of PEFT: Towards Million Personal Models of Trillion Parameters
nodes.author: Mind Lab
nodes.rationale: Proposes three-axis framework (Scale Up, Scale Down, Scale Out) for understanding PEFT as mechanism for personal models built on shared foundation models with small local adapters

nodes.label: Scale Up: Strengthen the Shared Prior
nodes.rationale: Asks whether stronger shared base models make small local updates more useful; addresses prior-limited nature of RL and how LoRA enables budgeted access to strong priors

nodes.label: Scale Down: Shrink the Adaptive State
nodes.rationale: Asks how small the local adaptive state can become while still learning reliably; focuses on rank regimes, initialization, and hyperparameter transfer

nodes.label: Scale Out: Sustain a Persistent Population
nodes.rationale: Asks what becomes possible when many persistent adapted instances coexist; examines LoRA memory capacity, per-user adapter simulation, and diversity-based aggregation

nodes.label: Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning (PEFT)
nodes.rationale: Core mechanism for representing persistent local adaptive state on top of shared foundation models; enables small trainable adapters to carry instance-specific behavioral state

nodes.label: Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA)
nodes.rationale: Specific PEFT method that freezes pretrained weights and injects trainable low-rank matrices; enables budgeted access to strong priors by reducing trainable parameters while preserving shared base model

nodes.label: RL is Prior-Limited
nodes.rationale: Core observation that RL effectiveness depends on base model's ability to sample useful trajectories; stronger models make RL more productive by assigning probability mass to useful but unstable behaviors

nodes.label: Trillion-Scale LoRA RL
nodes.rationale: Demonstrates operationalization of LoRA-based RL on trillion-parameter MoE models; requires co-design of adapter placement, rollout generation, and distributed optimization

nodes.label: Training-Inference Mismatch (TIM)
nodes.rationale: Scale-induced algorithmic failure where policy used for rollout differs from policy optimized during training; in MoE models, can alter expert routing and change effective computation

nodes.label: Router Replay R3
nodes.rationale: Mechanism to address TIM in sparse MoE architectures by recording and replaying routing decisions during training to preserve sampled computation

nodes.label: MinT: Mind Lab Infrastructure
nodes.author: Mind Lab, 2026
nodes.rationale: Concrete infrastructure example supporting all three scaling axes; provides adapter identity, policy revision, training provenance, evaluation, and serving residency mechanisms

nodes.label: Personal Model Instance
nodes.rationale: System built from shared base model, local adaptive state (adapter), context, tools, and external memory; carries learned consequences of repeated experience such as preferences, skills, and tool habits

nodes.label: Foundation Model (Shared Prior)
nodes.rationale: Strong shared base model that supplies broad intelligence and common competence; enables small local updates to be high-leverage by providing richer latent structure to redirect

nodes.label: Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) Architecture
nodes.rationale: Sparse architecture used in frontier models; introduces expert routing and discrete computation paths that create scale-induced failure modes in PEFT-based RL

nodes.label: GRPO: On-Policy RL Optimization
nodes.rationale: On-policy optimization loop used in trillion-scale LoRA RL; makes system a reinforcement learning loop rather than static supervised adapter update

nodes.label: Kimi K2 System
nodes.rationale: Proof-of-existence for trillion-parameter sparse prior adaptation; demonstrates LoRA RL on 1.04T parameter MoE model with 32.6B activated parameters using GRPO-style optimization

nodes.label: GLM5/GLM5.1 Support
nodes.rationale: Case study showing how sparse-architecture and adapter-semantics failures appear together; demonstrates that infrastructure becomes part of model definition at frontier scale

nodes.label: δ-mem: Stateful Adapter Design
nodes.rationale: Memory-oriented adapter design that accumulates interaction history; represents redesign of adaptive unit beyond static LoRA

nodes.label: LoRA Rank Regimes
nodes.rationale: Characterization of LoRA rank into low-rank research frontier, middle-rank deployment default, and high-rank cost-warning regimes; shows rank is not monotonic capacity curve

nodes.label: Context Learning
nodes.rationale: Write policy for personal adapters that enables context-to-parameter learning in persistent model instances

nodes.label: Diversity-Based Majority Voting
nodes.rationale: Aggregation mechanism for collective intelligence; demonstrates that diversity among distinct LoRA variants produces measurable performance gains

nodes.label: DeepSeek-R1-Zero
nodes.author: DeepSeek-AI, 2025
nodes.rationale: Demonstrates that large-scale RL can elicit reasoning behaviors without relying solely on supervised reasoning traces; supports prior-limited view of RL

nodes.label: Open-Reasoner-Zero
nodes.author: Hu et al., 2025a
nodes.rationale: Shows that simple on-policy RL recipes improve reasoning when applied to sufficiently capable base model; supports prior-limited view

nodes.label: LoRA Forgetting and Representation Movement Study
nodes.author: Biderman et al., 2024
nodes.rationale: Demonstrates that LoRA forgets less than full fine-tuning and differs in representation movement; advantageous for personal models that must preserve base capabilities

nodes.label: LoRA vs Full Fine-Tuning Equivalence Study
nodes.author: Shuttleworth et al., 2025
nodes.rationale: Shows LoRA and full fine-tuning are not equivalent in representation movement; cautions against treating LoRA as simple substitute for full training

nodes.label: LoRA: Low-Rank Adaptation of Large Language Models
nodes.author: Hu et al., 2021
nodes.rationale: Original LoRA proposal; foundational work for parameter-efficient fine-tuning approach used throughout paper

nodes.label: ENCODE Project: Regulatory DNA in Organisms
nodes.author: ENCODE Project Consortium, 2012
nodes.rationale: Provides biological analogy showing regulatory DNA increases from ~10% in simple organisms to 98% in humans; motivates Scale Up axis

nodes.label: 1000 Genomes Project: Human Genetic Variation
nodes.author: 1000 Genomes Project Consortium et al., 2012
nodes.rationale: Shows humans share >99.9% of genome; provides biological analogy for Scale Down and Scale Out axes

nodes.label: Retrieval-Augmented Generation
nodes.author: Lewis et al., 2021
nodes.rationale: Cited as complementary mechanism to PEFT for preserving continuity; personal models combine adapters with retrieval systems

nodes.label: Memory Systems for Language Models
nodes.author: Packer et al., 2024
nodes.rationale: Cited as external memory system; PEFT adapters complement rather than replace external memory

nodes.author: Zhong et al., 2024
nodes.rationale: Cited as external memory system; PEFT adapters complement rather than replace external memory

nodes.label: PEFT Rank Reduction and RL-Native Initialization Study
Rank Reduction Under Minimal Parameters
nodes.rationale: Central question in PEFT: whether useful learning survives under extreme rank reduction; LoRA rank defines an adaptation regime rather than a simple capacity knob.

nodes.label: Three Distinct Rank Operating Regions
nodes.rationale: Empirical sweep on Qwen3-8B PPO (216 runs) reveals behavior separates into three regions: middle-rank (r=16–32, strongest practical balance), low-rank (r=1–4, best-run competitive but unreliable mean), high-rank (r≥64, inflated footprint without frontier extension).

nodes.label: Mean–Best Performance Separation
nodes.rationale: Best-seed frontier remains nearly flat across ranks 1–32, while across-seed mean drops at low rank; indicates optimization/initialization bottleneck rather than hard capacity limit.

nodes.label: Reliability vs. Capacity Distinction
nodes.rationale: Low-rank limitation is reliability (seed-to-seed variance) rather than expressivity; best runs at rank 1 match ranks 16–32, but mean performance and consistency collapse.

nodes.label: RL-Native Initialization Criterion
nodes.rationale: Initialization must expose meaningful low-dimensional learning direction without making first policy updates too large; differs from supervised fine-tuning because RL operates under KL-constrained trust region where early policy movement is exponentially unstable.

nodes.label: KL Leash: Policy-Space Trust Region
nodes.rationale: Policy-space trust region induces weight-space movement budget; RL fine-tuning must make progress through small controlled steps, not large jumps; bad initialization can push optimizer toward directions where small parameter movements create large policy drift.

nodes.label: OLoRA-tail: Controlled Geometry Initialization
nodes.rationale: Initializes from minor singular vectors (U_{-r}, V_{-r}) without singular-value scaling; preserves pretrained geometry while avoiding destabilizing scaling that SVD methods (PiSSA, MiLoRA) introduce; designed for RL stability by keeping adapter updates orthogonal to sensitive weight directions.

nodes.label: LoRA: Low-Rank Adaptation
nodes.rationale: Standard baseline; initializes adapter direction randomly; sufficient at moderate ranks but becomes unreliable at rank r=1 due to single-direction collapse.

nodes.label: PiSSA: Principal Singular Subspace Adaptation
nodes.rationale: Initializes adapters using principal singular directions; effective in supervised fine-tuning but exhibits training collapse in RL with verifiable rewards due to large distributional shifts.

nodes.label: MiLoRA: Minor Singular Subspace Adaptation
nodes.rationale: Uses minor singular directions with singular-value scaling; can be effective in supervised fine-tuning but may underperform in RL; OLoRA-tail removes the scaling component for stability.

nodes.label: OLoRA: Orthogonal LoRA (Principal)
nodes.rationale: Initializes from principal singular vectors; undergoes training collapse under DAPO objective (reward drops to −1.0, KL divergence explodes to ~8 by step 100) because principal subspace captures dominant pretrained directions whose perturbation induces large distributional shifts.

nodes.label: Qwen3-8B PPO Rank Sweep
nodes.rationale: 216 runs across 9 LoRA ranks, 4 batch sizes, 6 seeds; fixed 500-step PPO schedule on mixed mathematics corpus with verifiable rewards; primary evidence for three-region behavior.

nodes.label: DAPO 1.5B Initialization Comparison
nodes.rationale: DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-1.5B trained with DAPO; compares LoRA, PiSSA, MiLoRA, OLoRA, OLoRA-tail over 500 steps; demonstrates PiSSA/MiLoRA collapse and OLoRA-tail stability.

nodes.label: Rank-1 OLoRA-tail vs LoRA on Qwen3-8B
nodes.rationale: Batch size sweep at rank r=1; OLoRA-tail maintains ~+20% gain across all batch sizes (bs16–bs128), while LoRA degrades from +15% to −18% with 67% collapse risk.

nodes.label: Rank-1 OLoRA-tail on Qwen3-30B-A3B-Instruct
nodes.rationale: OLoRA-tail achieves 35.5% ± 1.6% average pass rate vs LoRA 24.0%, a +11.5 percentage point (+48% relative) improvement.

nodes.label: Rank-16 OLoRA-tail on Mathematical Reasoning
nodes.rationale: DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-1.5B trained with DAPO on DAPO-Math-17k; OLoRA-tail achieves 58.3% average accuracy vs LoRA 56.3% across GSM8K, MATH500, AIME22–25.

nodes.label: Sequence-Level RLVR Objective
nodes.rationale: J(θ) = E[R(x,y)] where R ∈ {0,1} assigned to complete response; importance-weighted form exhibits exponential instability (e.g., 1.01^512 ≈ 163); token-level surrogates depend on first-order Taylor expansion accurate only when policies remain close.

nodes.label: Importance-Sampling Exponential Instability
nodes.rationale: Sequence-level importance weight decomposes as product of token-level ratios; exponentially unstable when sequence length T is large; explains why RL fine-tuning is sensitive to early policy movement.

nodes.label: Personal Models Scale-Down Objective
nodes.rationale: Rank reduction compounds across repeated updates, optimizer states, checkpoints, serving-time loads, and millions of persistent model instances; goal is to keep population close to 'share 99.5%, differ in 0.5%' regime for economic feasibility.

nodes.label: Batch Size as Budget Variable
nodes.rationale: Larger batches increase token consumption under fixed-step PPO schedule; slightly improve average gain but increase downside risk; not a pure optimization knob but part of broader score–cost tradeoff.

nodes.label: Seed-Heavy Evaluation for Reliability
nodes.rationale: Cheaper adapters enable repeated experimentation (seed-heavy evaluation, stronger initialization, cleaner schedules, tighter KL control, rank-specific hyperparameters); broader evidence collection turns lucky low-rank runs into reliable ones.

nodes.label: High-Rank Opportunity Cost
nodes.rationale: Beyond middle-rank region (r≥64), adapter footprint increases while performance frontier flattens; unnecessary rank displaces more useful expenditures (additional seeds, ablations, variance control, reward debugging).

nodes.label: DAPO-Math-17k Dataset
nodes.rationale: Mixed mathematics corpus with verifiable rewards used for DAPO training experiments.

nodes.label: GSM8K Mathematical Reasoning Benchmark
nodes.rationale: Evaluation benchmark for mathematical reasoning; used to compare LoRA and OLoRA-tail.

nodes.label: MATH500 Benchmark
nodes.rationale: Mathematical reasoning benchmark; used to evaluate OLoRA-tail vs LoRA.

nodes.label: AIME Benchmarks (2022–2025)
nodes.rationale: American Invitational Mathematics Examination benchmarks (AIME22, AIME23, AIME24, AIME25); used for comprehensive mathematical reasoning evaluation.

nodes.label: Qwen3-8B Model
nodes.rationale: 8B parameter model used for PPO rank sweep and rank-1 OLoRA-tail experiments.

nodes.label: Qwen3-30B-A3B-Instruct Model
nodes.rationale: 30B parameter instruction-tuned model used for rank-1 OLoRA-tail evaluation.

nodes.label: DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-1.5B Model
nodes.rationale: 1.5B distilled model used for initialization method comparisons and mathematical reasoning evaluation.

nodes.label: DAPO: Direct Advantage Policy Optimization
nodes.rationale: RL training objective used throughout experiments; employs clipping mechanism and KL penalties to maintain trust region; sensitive to early policy movement.

nodes.label: REINFORCE Gradient Distribution
nodes.rationale: REINFORCE distributes sequence-level reward across token positions; forms basis for token-level surrogate objectives in RL fine-tuning.

nodes.label: First-Order Taylor Expansion for Token-Level Surrogates
nodes.rationale: Token-level surrogates depend on first-order Taylor expansion; accurate only when rollout and updated policies remain close; dropping higher-order terms gives approximate token-level objective.

nodes.label: KL Divergence Second-Order Bound
nodes.rationale: If D_KL(π_{θ+} ∥ π_θ) ≤ K and F(θ) ⪰ mI on update subspace, then block update obeys KL constraint; creates weight-space movement budget from policy-space trust region.

nodes.label: Minor Subspace Safety Property
nodes.rationale: Minor singular vectors span directions comparatively inert in pretrained model; adapter updates remain orthogonal to most sensitive weight directions, keeping KL divergence near zero and training stable.

nodes.label: Principal Subspace Distributional Shift Risk
nodes.rationale: Principal subspace captures dominant pretrained directions; perturbation through on-policy RL updates induces large distributional shifts that DAPO clipping cannot fully contain; explains OLoRA collapse.

nodes.label: Rank vs. Initialization Tradeoff
nodes.rationale: Rank determines number of available directions; initialization determines whether those directions are usable; in tiny-adapter regime, choosing direction geometrically can be strictly more parameter-efficient than adding rank.

nodes.label: Usable Capacity vs. Trainable Parameters
nodes.rationale: OLoRA-tail improves adapter's usable capacity without increasing trainable weights, optimizer state, checkpoint size, or serving-time footprint; enables scale-down for personal model populations.

nodes.label: Scale Out: Population-Scale Personalization
nodes.author: Mind Lab
nodes.rationale: Scale Out addresses how diversity among adapted models becomes a computational resource through collective intelligence; diversity itself is the scaling variable, not just throughput.

nodes.label: Scale Up: Large-Prior LoRA RL
nodes.author: Mind Lab
nodes.rationale: Scale Up makes the shared base model worth adapting by keeping expensive dense or MoE bases resident while LoRA adapters remain trainable and reusable.

nodes.label: Scale Down: Adapter-Only Mobility
nodes.author: Mind Lab
nodes.rationale: Scale Down ensures each update remains small and stable by exporting adapter revisions rather than merged checkpoints, enabling reusability across training, rollout, evaluation, and serving.

nodes.label: Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning (PEFT)
nodes.author: Mind Lab
nodes.rationale: PEFT is the foundational technique enabling all three scaling axes; it makes individuality compact and persistent adaptation efficient.

nodes.label: Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA)
nodes.author: Mind Lab
nodes.rationale: LoRA is the specific PEFT mechanism used; per-user LoRA adapters carry distinct learned policies shaped by different interaction histories, addressing the collapse problem of prompt-based user simulation.

nodes.label: MinT: Managed Infrastructure for PEFT Populations
nodes.author: Mind Lab
nodes.rationale: MinT is the systems layer that operationalizes the three scaling axes by managing policy records, adapter revisions, serving residency, and lifecycle state.

nodes.label: OASIS: Open Agent Social Interaction Simulations
nodes.author: Mind Lab
nodes.rationale: OASIS is used as the evaluation environment for testing per-user LoRA adapters against shared-base agents in social simulation; demonstrates that adapter diversity produces richer interaction topology.

nodes.label: User Simulator as World Model
nodes.author: Mind Lab
nodes.rationale: Personal models become part of the environment experienced by other agents; a good user simulator acts as a world model for user reactions, preferences, constraints, and long-term behavior.

nodes.label: Diversity as Collective Intelligence
nodes.author: Mind Lab
nodes.rationale: Once many adaptive instances coexist, diversity itself becomes a computational resource; different personal models accumulate distinct histories, specialize along different trajectories, and solve problems through different reasoning paths.

nodes.label: Model-Count Scaling Law
nodes.author: Mind Lab
nodes.rationale: Accuracy improves approximately linearly in ln(k) where k is model count; collaboration across distinct LoRA models improves beyond repeated sampling from one model, indicating complementary policies.

nodes.label: Policy Record: Durable Identity of Adapted Behavior
nodes.author: Mind Lab
nodes.rationale: Policy records make an adapted behavior resumable, auditable, and rollbackable by recording base version, LoRA rank, target modules, checkpoints, rollout records, and exported revisions.

nodes.label: Adapter Revision: Fixed Serving/Evaluation Object
nodes.author: Mind Lab
nodes.rationale: Adapter revisions are fixed exported PEFT adapters in serving tensor layout; they define behavior selected by rollout, evaluation, serving, and rollback.

nodes.label: Serving Residency: Three-Tier Placement
nodes.author: Mind Lab
nodes.rationale: MinT separates serving state into durable catalog, CPU cache, and GPU batch; policy identity is stable across all three placements while only residency changes.

nodes.label: Context Learning: In-Context Improvement to Persistent Behavior
nodes.author: Mind Lab
nodes.rationale: Context Learning needs a path from context-time improvement to future query-only behavior; requires identity, provenance, mobility, and residency control.

nodes.label: Skill Internalization: Tool Outcomes to Adapter State
nodes.author: Mind Lab
nodes.rationale: Skill internalization needs repeated updates from tool outcomes and failures; requires writeable local state and path from experience to durable adapter state.

nodes.label: Personalization as Security Boundary
nodes.author: Mind Lab
nodes.rationale: Personalization as security boundary requires permission and behavior history to remain attached to policy that will later act; needs identity and provenance.

nodes.label: Qwen3 Models: Large-Scale Base Models
nodes.author: Mind Lab
nodes.rationale: Qwen3-30B and Qwen3-235B are used as base models for Scale Up experiments; demonstrate large-prior LoRA RL with computation provenance.

nodes.label: Kimi K2: 1T-Parameter MoE Model
nodes.author: Mind Lab
nodes.rationale: Kimi K2 1T-class countdown-task LoRA RL run demonstrates Scale Up on frontier-scale MoE with 32.6B active parameters.
